items.title: Cancelling a Shipped order returns 409 with the domain message
covers: Expected: 409 for cancel on Shipped order
items.reason: This is the exact reproduction from the bug (order 5, Shipped): it returned 500 and must now be a client error. Functional layer because the whole path (endpoint, MediatR, IdentifiedCommandHandler, EF, domain exception) must be exercised against a real database.

items.title: Cancelling a Paid order returns 409
covers: Implementation Notes: Cancel on a Paid or Shipped order -> 409
items.reason: `SetCancelledStatus` rejects both Paid and Shipped; Shipped is covered by TC-BUG-10-01, so Paid is a separate branch of the same rule.

items.title: Shipping an order that is not Paid returns 409
covers: Implementation Notes: Ship on an order that is not Paid -> 409
items.reason: `SetShippedStatus` only allows Paid. Ship is a separate endpoint from cancel and was equally mapped to 500, so it needs its own case.

items.title: Shipping an already Shipped order returns 409
covers: Implementation Notes: Ship on an order that is not Paid -> 409
items.reason: Boundary of the "only Paid can ship" rule: the state after a successful ship must itself be rejected, not silently accepted.

items.title: Cancelling an order that does not exist returns 404
items.reason: The suggested fix requires 404 for a missing order. The existing functional test `CancelNonExistentOrderFails` asserts 500 and must be updated to 404.

items.title: Shipping an order that does not exist returns 404
items.reason: Same rule on the ship endpoint; existing `ShipNonExistentOrderFails` asserts 500 and must become 404.

items.title: Cancel with an empty request id returns 400 before the order lookup
covers: Implementation Notes: x-requestid check runs first
items.reason: The notes say the `x-requestid` check runs first. Using a non-existent order proves ordering: it must be 400, not 404.

items.title: Ship with an empty request id returns 400 before the order lookup
covers: Implementation Notes: x-requestid check runs first
items.reason: Same ordering rule on the ship endpoint.

items.title: Cancelling a Submitted order still returns 200 and cancels it
covers: Valid cancel still succeeds (regression guard for the new exception handling)
items.reason: Guards that rethrowing domain exceptions and the new existence check did not break the valid path.

items.title: Shipping a Paid order still returns 200 and ships it
items.reason: Guards the valid ship path after the same changes.

items.title: CancelOrderAsync maps OrderingDomainException to Conflict
items.reason: Cheapest layer to pin the mapping and the detail text: `OrdersWebApiTest` already calls endpoint methods with a substituted `IMediator`.

items.title: ShipOrderAsync maps OrderingDomainException to Conflict
items.reason: Separate method from cancel with its own try/catch.

items.title: Cancel and ship return NotFound without sending a command when the order is missing
items.reason: Pins that the lookup guards the command, so a missing order never reaches the mediator.

items.title: A false command result still returns 500 for cancel and ship
covers: Implementation Notes: other command failures still return 500
items.reason: Story states other failures stay 500; guards against over-broad 4xx mapping.

items.title: IdentifiedCommandHandler rethrows OrderingDomainException
items.reason: This is the root change that lets the endpoint see the rule violation; `IdentifiedCommandHandlerTest` already exists for it.

items.title: IdentifiedCommandHandler still returns default for other exceptions
covers: Deviations: other exceptions still return default
items.reason: Non-domain faults must keep their old behavior (and so a 500 at the endpoint).

items.title: CreateOrderAsync still returns Ok when a domain exception is thrown
items.reason: Rethrowing in the shared handler could leak into create order, which BUG-9 owns; it must keep returning 200.
